### N20. Curves, singular coefficients and rationality of L-functions

“Il semble que pour les courbes, on récupère … (sans résolution des singularités) … $\rightsquigarrow$ rationalité des fonctions $L$” is a proposed application of the formalism, not a proved curve theorem on this page. A proof would have to identify the extension-by-zero or immersion argument, justify the local terms for the singular coefficient sheaf, and then pass from the trace identities to the Euler product/determinant identity. The finished SGA 5 provides distinct comparison destinations for Lefschetz and for rationality, but the present evidence does not identify this draft with a particular circulated version (Grothendieck, 1977, Exposé III; Illusie, 1977, volume contents).
### N21. Formalism is deliberately prioritized over applications

The insertion “th. de bidualité (= dualité locale)” and the sentence “je préfère en compléter les lignes essentielles” locate the author's next work within a chosen formal programme rather than an exhausted list of applications. The juxtaposition of Lefschetz–Cartier and rationality is a research lead, but the overlapping cancellations prevent a confident reconstruction of every proposed transition. This adds manuscript evidence for the README's SGA 4/5 placement while differing in subject from the Hodge-index use of “Lefschetz” in **WG H9**.

“Il ne serait pas admissible de se limiter à des corps” makes the arithmetic objective explicit: the author wants information finer than the fixed-point count modulo $\ell$. The obstruction is that cohomology modules over $\mathbb Z/\ell^\nu\mathbb Z$ need not be free, so the usual degreewise finite-projective trace cannot simply be applied to each of them. The subsequent Bourbaki/$\ell$-adic discussion is a workaround under consideration, whereas 128–136 introduces a finite-level complex-theoretic construction; neither passage is a withdrawal of the demand for integral information.
### N24. The finite-level-to-adic passage is an expectation

“On a envie de dire … conséquence formelle, par passage à la limite” proposes deriving the adic formula from finite-level trace identities. To make that claim precise one needs compatible coefficient reduction, an appropriate inverse-limit formalism and control of finiteness; the draft supplies no full inverse-limit argument here. The supplied results register has no entry settling this passage, and the clipped upper addition cannot be used to infer a stronger integrality assertion than the legible text supports.

The words “d'additivité pour un mapping cylindre” should be read with their chain-level compatibility data, not promoted to additivity for every endomorphism of an abstract distinguished triangle. The latter statement is false even for perfect complexes: The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 087L](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087L), Lemma 110.65.1) gives a counterexample. This is a boundary for a possible modern reconstruction, not a contradiction of what the manuscript actually states.

“Remarque sur changement de base non plat” replaces the earlier flatness restriction by a derived pullback defined through flat resolutions, followed on 106 by transitivity “sans hypothèse sur $f,g$ composables.” Relative to 102, this adds a broader construction; it does not retract the flat special case or license replacing every visible $f^*$ by $\mathbb Lf^*$. The modern comparison is the monoidal and compositional structure in The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 06YV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YV), Lemmas 21.18.3–4).

The “Formule de projection” on this sheet is the derived internal-Hom comparison, supported by the external-Hom adjunction and the assertion that the localization square permits the needed base change. Its proof obligation is compatibility of those constructions with restriction to the indicated localizations, not an arbitrary base-change theorem for every square. This adds a local-to-global proof strategy to the supplied plan; no corresponding assertion or scan is present in the context register.

“C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The finite-type-over-a-field case has a direct modern counterpart (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0F10](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10)), and Illusie (2014, Exposé XVIII_A, Corollary 1.4) proves the relative $\ell$-torsion statement for finite-dimensional noetherian $Y$ with $\ell$ invertible on $Y$. Those results confirm qualified versions; these notes leave the draft's full “merely noetherian” scope unresolved and do not offer the absolute cohomology of a field as a counterexample to it.

“Il faut vérifier que c'est un hom fonctoriel pour les catégories dérivées” explicitly leaves a verification after constructing the comparison on resolutions. The subsequent reductions to degree-zero terms and an étale generator, and the marginal proposal to use proper base change on geometric fibres, address why the comparison should be an isomorphism but do not themselves supply every naturality and resolution-independence diagram. This adds a precise unfinished compatibility problem to the README's S19 comparison programme.

The argument beginning “si $X$ ou $Y$ propre sur $k$” combines proper base change with projection and is explicitly distinguished on 120 from statements requiring $n$ prime to the characteristic. The Stacks Project Authors (n.d., [Tag 0F14](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F14), Lemma 59.97.2(2)) confirms this one-proper-factor formula for finite-type schemes over a separably closed field and arbitrary $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ complexes, without assuming $n$ invertible. This comparison supports the manuscript's distinction rather than transferring the later prime-to-characteristic condition backwards to all Künneth formulas in the package.

A concrete check of “même si $X$ … un pt géométrique” is $A=\mathbb Z/\ell^2\mathbb Z$ and $M=A/\ell A$: the resolution with every differential multiplication by $\ell$ is exact, while tensoring it with $M$ makes every differential zero. This is our elementary example, adding an explicit witness to the manuscript's warning, not a claim that the example is written there.
### N19. The locally constant variant needs its actual scope

“Une démonstration presque immédiate” reduces the locally constant-cohomology variant to $M=A_Y$, but the paragraph stops at “où” and does not display the whole dévissage. A secure overlapping theorem is projection for a perfect target complex over any morphism of ringed topoi (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 0944](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0944)); this does not by itself settle the manuscript's broader finite-cohomological-dimension/locally-constant variant over a nonregular finite ring. In particular, the finite module in N10 is locally constant at a point and pseudo-coherent there, yet not perfect, so these hypotheses must not be conflated.

“C'est peut-être vrai dès que $Y$ est noethérien” concerns finite **relative** cohomological dimension of $f_*$, in the surrounding finite-type discussion, rather than finite absolute cohomological dimension of $Y$. The manuscript uses one fixed interval for “tout pt géom,” a quantifier that should be retained in any reconstruction. On a disjoint union of infinitely many points, put a copy of $A$ in cohomological degree $-n$ on the $n$th component: this is locally perfect and bounded above, with finite Tor-amplitude at every stalk, but it has no single global finite amplitude interval. The example distinguishes the manuscript's uniform claim from the local perfectness criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 08G8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08G8)); it does not refute the fixed-interval stalkwise criterion on the page.

The inserted hypothesis “l'Anneau de base soit de torsion” belongs to the proposition, whose proof is described as “Résulte … de Künneth.” For compactifiable $f$ with geometric fibres of dimension at most $d$, Deligne (1973, XVII, Corollary 5.2.8.1 and Proposition 5.2.9) gives $\mathrm{cd}(Rf_!)\leq2d$ for torsion sheaves and the projection comparison. Our inference sends Tor-amplitude $[a,b]$ in cohomological indexing into $[a,b+2d]$; setting $a=-M,b=-N$ then yields the displayed homological $[N-2d,M]$. This supports the direction of the shift without imposing a prime-to-characteristic hypothesis absent from this compact-support argument.
